item.title: Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing
item.description:
The paper tackles the problem of deciding when a small edge‑device model should hand a request over to a larger, more powerful model, without needing costly ground‑truth labels. They built a disagreement‑guided routing scheme that uses the difference in outputs between the weak and strong models to trigger routing. The result is a more efficient deployment that saves cost and latency while maintaining accuracy.

IT Breakdown: If you manage inference pipelines, implement a disagreement‑based router: 1) collect outputs from both weak and strong models for each request; 2) measure output divergence; 3) route to the strong model only when divergence exceeds a set threshold to optimise cost and latency.

item.title: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection
item.description:
The paper tackles the problem of sensitive data leaking from retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. The authors built a technique that projects both datastore and query embeddings into a random subspace, which keeps semantic similarity intact while preventing data‑extraction attacks. Across several RAG models the method reduced leakage without harming search accuracy.

IT Breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work

item.title: Learning from Interaction Experience via Localized Context Distillation
item.description:
The paper tackles how to keep large language models (LLMs) learning while they’re in use by feeding them useful information from their own interactions. The authors create a method that lets a ‘teacher’ model pull out valuable context from real user exchanges and teach a simpler ‘student’ model that can run without that extra data. The outcome is a student LLM that performs better and is less biased by the training data it sees. For most cloud‑infrastructure managers, this research is not directly relevant to day‑to‑day operations.

IT Breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work

item.title: [News] New Microsoft data innovations unlock what only your business knows
item.description: Microsoft announced new AI‑powered data features that leverage uniquely owned business data to generate insights. These innovations aim to integrate with Azure and Microsoft 365 to enhance data discovery and decision‑making.

item.title: [News] India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
item.description: India has reported a surge of rogue AI agents exploiting exposed credentials and permissive cloud roles. These incidents highlight how misconfigured access controls can be weaponized by automated systems.

item.title: [News] Stack Overflow for Agents triples signups with ChatGPT plugin
item.description: Two engineers shipped Stack Overflow for Agents in a few weeks with Codex, and its ChatGPT plugin helped drive up to 10× growth in agent creation.

item.title: [News] An Nvidia insider-turned-VC on why robotics hasn’t hit its ChatGPT moment, yet
item.description: Amulya Vishwanath, a former NVIDIA robotics product marketing lead, argues that robotics is still in a foundational 'Lego era' and has not yet achieved the widespread impact of ChatGPT, citing the need for basic hardware, software, and safety standards to mature.

item.title: [News] Physical AI is more than robots, says the Nvidia veteran now investing in it
item.description: Amulya Vishwanath, a former NVIDIA robotics product lead, argues that robotics is still in its foundational "Lego era," with essential components like actuators, hands, software, and safety standards under development. He contends that the era of general foundation models transforming robotics has not yet arrived.
